abstract: Abnormal placental attachment disorders are less common than abnormal placental position disorders, but they are a significant cause of mortality and morbidity. The diagnosis is usually made by an ultrasound examination, but for the equivocal cases, MRI increases the diagnostic certitude. The purpose of our study was to determine if conventional MRI combined with Diffusion Weighted Imaging and image post-processing techniques using Fusion of the images could improve the current MRI diagnosis protocol.

articleTitle: Web based application for improving the education quality of young medical genetics healthcare professionals
abstract: Karyotyping is one of the skills geneticists should master in their formation. The way this ability is developed nowadays is time consuming for both the fellow and the coordinator. We created an application to forward/advance the process. Using images captured by Zeiss Axio Imager.N1 and sorted in karyograms with the Ikaros v5.2.8 software, with the help of HTML, CSS, JavaScript, SQL, PHP scripting language we developed an educational software for medical genetics fellows. The internet based application aids in the karyotyping learning of new geneticists. It has a theory section, MCQ tests based on the content and hands on learning on how to recognize and pair the chromosomes. Using a simple drag and drop system the program stops you from misplacing the chromosomes. It counts the number of false positioning attempts and the time you spend on each test, giving you a progress evaluation feedback. At the end of each test a pop up message appears containing the particularity of the arranged chromosome set (e.g.: deletion, inversions, duplications etc.). The application can be accessed at http://optimx.ro/ool/. This tool will help the future generation of geneticists develop their skills faster and give them more flexibility in their schedule.

articleTitle: Interaction schemes for the analysis of combined action of risk factors
abstract: The risk factors analysis in medicine is a very complex problem, with significant practical implications in taking the right decisions in the health policies field. A useful approach is the study of interaction between risk factors through additive and multiplicative schemes, required when the identified risk factors are not independent in causing a certain outcome. Several models were developed to solve this problem, but it is critical to choose the right one, because different methods can lead to different conclusions about the same biological processes. Our paper describes the additive and multiplicative interaction schemes and presents a practical application of them in investigating the effects of a few particular diet habits on the chances to develop gingival recession, on a sample made from 2389 people coming from Iasi county. 8 diet habits were investigated; only 4 of them were identified as risk factors and, among the 6 possible paired combinations, 4 were identified as major positive interaction, 1 was identified as moderate interaction and 1 was identified as weak.

articleTitle: Smart guiding system for medical care buildings
abstract: The work of this paper is done within the context of European Project E! 9770 i-Light, which aims at developing intelligent systems based on smart luminaries for building monitoring. The work presented in this paper extends the work from i-Light project towards a smart guiding system for buildings. The system is based on the use of smart luminaries and drones. One of the main targets of such a system is medical care units. Use case scenarios include: give audio indications to potential users (patients, visitors, etc.), carrying relevant supplies to the desired location, etc. This paper will discuss the components of the system localization techniques applied within a building.

articleTitle: Assessment of cervical disk prosthesis by means of video-fluoroscopy image processing
abstract: Many cervical spine pathologies involve degeneration of the stabilizing mechanisms of vertebrae segments and often cause pain. Abnormal intervertebral motion is an indication for surgery. Currently, spinal fusion surgery is widely adopted to fix the instable vertebral segments but recently, disk arthroplasty is more and more adopted as an alternative to restore normal kinematics and biomechanics of the sick segment and to reduce development of symptomatic adjacent-level degeneration. This study aims to measure intervertebral kinematics by means of image processing of X-ray fluoroscopy videos, which are able to screen patient's neck spontaneous movements of flexion-extension. Vertebrae trajectories are estimated by using image template matching techniques. Then, continuous-time intervertebral kinematics is computed by using spline interpolation. The results, obtained by using real fluoroscopy videos, reveal the possibility of obtaining in vivo information about the continuous evolution of motion of the implanted prosthesis and adjacent segments.

articleTitle: Regularity assessment of cyclic human movements: An innovative method based on wearable sensors
abstract: This study aims at evaluating the regularity of periodic human movements through the analysis of the autocorrelation function of accelerometric signals obtained from wearable sensors. For this purpose a method has been implemented which can run also in real-time, and it has been tested in several experimental conditions and in various motor gestures including gait. Relevant for clinical and sport applications is the fact that the autocorrelation parameters are calculated on the acceleration module, and not on the individual axial components. This allowed us to assess the regularity of periodic movements without the need of aligning the sensor axes to the anatomical axes. Finally a multi-sensor approach has been developed that can be used to simultaneously assess the regularity on different anatomical landmarks.

articleTitle: Scoliosis risk assessment in children with pelvic asymmetry - a simple screening test based on gluteal area asymmetry
abstract: Very strong recent researches offer details about pelvic asymmetry and its pattern of growth. Asymmetric growth of the ilium bone from birth to adolescence and its statistical incidence besides asymmetric growing of other bodies' parts incidence impose the necessity to design a simple test for the risk of scoliosis due to pelvic or sacroiliac asymmetric disorders. The pelvis area is the base support of the spine so that the first factor in scoliosis is represented by the sacroiliac dysfunctions and the pelvis bones geometric asymmetry. The big issue is the time/the age when the scoliosis or the deformity is detected. A force platform was used to determine the pelvic repartition of pressure and the geometry of the pelvic perimeter on children with scoliosis risk. A measurement jig was designed to identify the volume difference between the left and right gluteus muscles due to difference in shape of left and right ilium bones. Based on the changes in the biomechanics of movement of the segments below the pelvis due to pelvis asymmetry, a squat exercise was designed for incipient detection of pelvic growth disorders. The exercises were proposed as a screening test. Beside the old Adam's test which is positive in the presence of a deformation, the exercises proposed, that can be completed by the gluteal geometric asymmetry, provide earlier information about the risk of scoliosis. Modern test were involved to support the proposal test, including a new method of force platform pelvimetry.

articleTitle: Oral rehabilitation with occlussal trays and adjuvants aerosols treatment in association with lasertherapy in pacients with dysfunctional syndrome of stomatognathic system and composite restoration
abstract: Physical kinetic therapy is a branch of medicine that uses natural and artificial physical factors in therapeutic purpose. The great number of these factors determined the dissemination between special therapeutic branches depending on the agent used: kinetic therapy, aerosols, massage therapy, laser therapy etc. The methods of physical therapy used in dental medicine represented an unknown and underappreciated domain for a long time. The systematization of these methods was accomplished in Iasi.

articleTitle: Application of biomedical technologies - issues in modern bioethics
abstract: The substantial increase of the medical needs in society triggered the development of various medical domains which generated a wide field for the applicability of biomedical technologies, and thus facilitated new perspectives in the worldwide management of important health issues. Biomedical technologies are a useful segment of contemporary medicine and an omnipresent component of modern society, while they also provide enough reasons in support of the assertion that their implementation in current health care should not be an exception. However, scientific progress maintained by application of biomedical technologies in research, treatment and prevention is challenged by several ethical and moral issues. Therefore, within the framework of ethical discussions regarding the impact of biomedical technologies, the emphasis placed on the moral qualities of technological interventions is equivalent with the interest to evaluate quantifiable medical consequencest.

articleTitle: Respiratory rate estimation using nostril detection in thermal video streams
abstract: In this paper we propose a complete method for breath rate estimation using thermal video streams and computer vision algorithms. The system performs subject nose detection, interest point extraction and tracking, geometric transformation and minimum thermal region estimation. All algorithms are carefully designed in order to ensure real-time capability on a regular desktop computer. The experimental evaluation validates the proposed methodology, when compared with traditional breath rate extraction methods, returning high accuracy scores.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the acrylic dental resins silver nanoparticles enriched
abstract: The prevention of dental stomatitis still represent a challenge for dentists and more studies are necessary in order to find the optimal prevention method. One of the direction is to take into consideration how silver nanoparticles could influence the structure of the resins and mechanical and physical properties. In our research we investigate the stress distribution in a dental acrylic resins reinforced with AgNps with 20 nm diameter in two concentration: 5 and 20% weight percent. In order to predict the optimum size and distribution of AgNps as average distance between particles, a finite element analysis was performed, revealing the stress field at the particle/matrix interface. Taking into consideration the conclusions it is obvious that the optimal AgNps concentration is 5%, from both biological and mechanical point of view.

articleTitle: Deterioration by friction on contact surfaces of the total knee prosthesis
abstract: In order to assess the wearing of polyethylene with high molecular density in knee prosthesis due to friction processes, a mathematical model of the forces at work has been developed.

articleTitle: Complex conservative treatment of chronic tonsillitis in children using local immunostimulation (autologous mononuclear cells)
abstract: Introduction. The priority directions in pediatric otorhinolaryngology are development of diagnostic criteria in chronic tonsillitis in children and argumentation of complex conservative therapy tactics to preserve palatine tonsils as important organs in local and general immunity. Materials and methods. The study included 64 children with chronic tonsillitis who were divided into 2 groups: 32 children were applied standard treatment including local immunomodulatory therapy (group 1) and 32 children - only standard treatment (group 2). Results. After treatment, sensitivity of T lymphocytes to streptococcus antigens and total content of B lymphocytes decreased more pronouncedly in children of group 1. Indices of T lymphocyte functional activity were conclusively increased in children of group 1 compared to children of lot 2. Local immunostimulation reduces supranormal levels of proinflammatory cytokines TNF-α, IL-S and IL-1β and increase the low titers of anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-4. Conclusions. Local therapy with autologous mononuclear cells has a complex action upon the changes of immune reactivity state in children with chronic tonsillitis.

articleTitle: Electrophysiology characteristics of middle ear in understanding of otitis media development in early childhood
abstract: During 10 years we monitored the middle ear status of 234 children since their first year of life till 10 years. Comparison of electro-acoustical and electrophysiological characteristics of middle ear in children suffered from otitis media and results of surgical interventions demonstrates high sensitivity of noninvasive methods to any pathological changes in middle ear. Analysis of monitoring results improves understanding of otitis media development in childhood.

Author Keywords: electro-acoustical and electrophysiological characteristics of middle ear

articleTitle: Esthetic landmarks in different types of prostheses correlated with the biomaterials structure
abstract: The aim of this study concerns the individualization of correlative aspects of the type of smile, teeth and visibility of how the therapeutic solution chosen, according to the particular clinical case provides ultimate clinical success through the aesthetic requirements. The analyzed group was represented by 40 patients, diagnosed with partial edentation; The sample was evaluated through descriptive statistics (performed in SPSS 20.0) and the smile type was emphasized by detecting the contours through image processing in Corel PhotoPaint 7.0. Regarding the type of smile met, we noted a prevalence of the convex-not contacting smile in a proportion of 35%, followed by smile convex-contacting and convex-covering, a rate of 25%, assuming the gingival smiles for a 15%. The therapeutic solutions which provided an optimal rehabilitation optimally were elected according to the established smile type. Beside the correctness of the clinical and technological maneuvers, the esthetic evaluation and the individualization of the esthetic area influence in a decisive way the final results.

articleTitle: Dentures and criteria of selection for their main connector - a clinical study
abstract: The main connector is an important component of the removable partial denture, a component related to all other elements of the dentures. The group of patients was represented by fifteen patients were randomly divided into three groups, each group consisting of five patients groups are designated as A, B and C, specific for palatal plate metal, palatal acrylic plate and palatal bar. Completed questionnaires showed that all three types of connectors affected speech, 40% of patients said they had been affected the process of chewing, and regarding swallowing, only 26.7% of patients were affected. The result of this study shows that the main connector metal bar was the main connector jaw accepted while the acrylic resin plate was less acceptable than metal plate main maxillary connector. It confirmed also influence of main connector design on to the future patient acceptance of denture.

articleTitle: Structural changes of the human saliva chemical composition at wearers of orthodontic appliances
abstract: Our experiment focused on identifying the elemental chemical composition of salivary crystals' surface, obtained from patients with/without orthodontic appliances or metal-ceramic crowns in order to test their influence on human saliva. We used 110 samples of saliva derived from 19 patients (11 males and 8 females), with ages between 11-26 years old, divided into three groups: the control sample (without orthodontic appliances/metal-ceramic crowns), the study sample A (with orthodontic appliances/physiognomic metal-ceramic crowns) and the study sample B (former patients with previous orthodontic appliances). The surface elemental chemical composition was observed through Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) and was analyzed by X-ray Energy Dispersive Spectroscopy (EDS). The statistical analysis was performed in SPSS 20.0. Metallic elements (Ni, Al, Zn) that do not derive from the chemical composition of human saliva were found on all the salivary crystals. There were found statistically significant differences for Ni between the study sample B and the control sample (p<;0.05). Our study found changes in the surface elemental chemical composition of crystallized human saliva. Orthodontic appliances applied in the oral cavity are not the main source of metallic elements released in the saliva, which is probably due to other causes from the investigated subjects' environment.

articleTitle: Surface roughness after finishing and polishing of a restorative nanocomposite material
abstract: The aim of the study was to evaluate the surface characteristics, after finishing and polishing with 3 different systems, of a universal nanocomposite material, starting from the microstructure experimentally analyzed by atomic force microscopy.

articleTitle: New methods of financing medical technology in the Czech Republic
abstract: Impact Financing funding models, namely Social Impact Bond and Impact Investing, are applied worldwide. However, they do not receive enough attention in the Czech Republic. The present study analyzes closely these methods, describes their functional principles and practices and illustrates them with process maps. Importantly, it is contextualized within the Czech conditions. The study includes an analysis of the application of these methods in the financing of medical technology, especially in the area of assistive technology in home care. At the end, a model is introduced designed for an efficient financing of the device designated for home artificial pulmonary ventilation. The study is supplemented by calculating the sensitivity analysis and the period necessary for the return of the initial investment.

articleTitle: A review of Romanian Space Agency's activity in the field of telemedicine and e-health
abstract: The Romanian Space Agency (ROSA) is the coordinator of Romania's national and international space activities. As a government institution, ROSA has concluded international agreements on behalf of the Romanian Government, including agreements with ESA and NASA. Between NASA and the Government of Romania, represented by ROSA, started in May 2000 a cooperation in the areas of Telemedicine and Telehealth, Agricultural research and Technology. This article will review ROSA's activity in the field of telemedicine and space applications in medicine highlighting the spin-offs including institutional outcome consisting in objectives of the National Strategy in this field. In 2001, thru the AEROSPATIAL National Research Programme was financed the first Telemedicine public pilot project in Romania, followed by several other projects and spin-offs, including telemedicine tests in remote areas as the Danube-Delta, which represented milestones in setting up the National Strategy in telemedicine and medical space applications, disaster management, communications, etc. Today, we find these objectives in the National Health Strategy 2014-2020 of the Ministry of Health (“development of e-medicine and higher accessibility to healthcare thru telemedicine”) and the National Strategy concerning Digital Agenda 2014-2020 for Romania of the Ministry of Communications (“e-medicine/support of ITC in health”), approved by the Romanian Government.

articleTitle: Glass fiber-reinforced dental bridges - clinical and mechanical properties
abstract: Bridges from composites reinforced with glass fibres are options for treating the absence of a single tooth, as a temporary but aesthetic solution for both anterior and lateral dental arch. This study aimed to determine clinical and mechanical properties of dental bridges using everStick C&B (GC) and Construct (Kerr) associated with GC Essentia Composite (GC Corporation, Japan) applied on four samples. The tests were done with the help of Universal Testing Machine, data recorded by a computer, and the evaluation of flexural strength and fatigue resistance revealed in specific diagrams. The fatigue resistance for bridges with FRC tested shown in diagrams, the force variations and the values of resistance in some points of each bridge. The tests demonstrate the possibility to increase endurance of such dental bridges, because the flexural strength and fatigue resistance are significantly increased by the fibres reinforcement (p <;0,001). The mechanical properties of the glass fibres reinforced composites evaluated show that FRCs are considerably stronger under the condition to enrich the matrix of FRC with glass fibre bundle type E for example, as there is GC everStick Crown & Bridge, which represent a perfect option to treat the space of one single tooth absence.

articleTitle: Retinal vessel labeling technique
abstract: A retinal vessel classification procedure is proposed. In a first step, from the thinned vessel image, a vascular graph is extracted and filtered. Then the graph edges near the optic disc are localized and the main branches connected to these initial edges are identified. For each graph with at least two starting branches, various label configurations are used to classify the graph's secondary edges (connected to the main ones). For each main branch, the initial label is first propagated along the branch edges, then along each secondary edge. The label propagation ends in case of conflicts at crossings. The no error label configuration or the one with the most classified edges is retained. The main improvement of the proposed technique is that the initial manual labeling for the starting vessels of each graph it is no longer necessary.

articleTitle: Determining the impact of the major prognostic factors in breast cancer
abstract: The paper presents a mathematical model of prognostic factors in breast cancer, accomplished for a determined period of 60 months. The study was conducted on a group of patients selected from all of the patients with breast cancer treated in the Clinic of Oncology-Radiation of Emergency Hospital “St. Spiridon” Iasi in a period of 3 years. Survival data specific for each prognostic factor was processed, from which resulted the survival curves at 5 years. Each resulting curve was approximated by a polynomial function. The prognostic score model, determined through the multifactorial analysis, assigns each patient a characteristic function of survival, with the possibility of calculating a specific value for a time moment selected as the reference.

articleTitle: Assessing potential dietary toxicity of heavy metals in lingonberry from Mănăila open-pit area (Suceava, Romania)
abstract: In this study, the content of heavy metals was determined in berries and leaves of lingonberry (Vaccinum vitisidaea) by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICPMS). Samples of lingonberry plant were collected from surroundings of open pit mining area of metallic sulphides bearing mineralization from Mănăila (Suceava County). On the base of legislative permissible limits, the berries and leaves show that the contamination is minimal for Cu, Zn and Pb, while a special attention should be paid to Mn content. The calculated health risk index is lower than unit for most of the heavy metals, except for Mn. This infers no risk of consumption since the fresh berries are used for a short period of time. If the berries and leaves are used for pharmaceutical extracts, the Mn effect would be diminished by mixing with those from uncontaminated areas. Generally, the lingonberries from Mănăila can be regarded as safety, as long as they are not used in daily dietary.

articleTitle: C-NAIL® - a new implant for minimally-invasive treatment of intraarticular calcaneal fractures
abstract: The treatment of dislocated intra-articular fractures of calcaneus gives a lot of debates between the orthopaedic surgeons. Minimally-invasive techniques beside offering good reduction of the fracture have lesser complications and for this reason tend to replace the open procedures. In this paper, we want to describe a new method of minimally-invasive technique used in the treatment of intra-articular calcaneal fractures and internal fixation with C-NAIL<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup>. The nail offers the possibility to insert up to seven screws into the calcaneus: two sustentacular screws, three latero-medial screws into the tuberosity and anterior process and 2 supero-inferior into the tuberosity. The first step of the procedure is the closed reduction of the calcaneal tuberosity to the sustentacular fragment and open reduction and internal fixation of the posterior facet through a 3-cm long incision made below the apex of the lateral malleolus. Second step in the insertion of the nail via a minimal incision just below the insertion of the Achille tendon. The nail and the screws creates an angularly stable fixation; the main stability is obtained by inserting the two screws into the sustentaculum.

articleTitle: Determination of deviation from spherical profile of total hip prosthesis
abstract: The paper presents a study in vitro concerning the deviation from sphericity of some components of total hip prosthesis (acetabular cups and femoral heads). Prosthesis have been tested on an experimental stand, on which were simulated the loads and movements from coxo-femoral articulation. Deviation from sphericity was determined in accordance with ASTM standards and specifications from the ISO on a CMM machine (MMC). Thus, the standard deviation of the sphericity was measured at the beginning of the tests (initial phase) during tests (intermediate phase) and at the end of the tests (final phase). Two types of articulation have been tested: metal on Metal (MoM) and Metal on Polyethylene (MoP). We believe that the sphericity deviation is a very important parameter in determining wear and loss of implant prosthetic components.

articleTitle: Rb protein dynamic modeling
abstract: Cancer is the second cause of death in developed countries after cardiovascular diseases. Our work serves in a better understanding of pRb-E2F process, a significant pathway of the cell cycle control and a frequent target of mutational events in the most human cancers. Using a mathematical model, the simulated phenomena that characterize the real system, preserves the logical structure, allowing to obtain information on process status at different moments of time.

articleTitle: Persistent bone edema, anterior tibial pain and delay in bone neo-formation associated with Poly-L-lactic acid screws fixation of the anterior cruciate ligament graft
abstract: The anterior cruciate ligament has quickly become one of the most reconstructed ligamentous structures in the human body. Graft fixation options have evolved and expanded with time, the market now having numerous possibilities. It can be clearly seen that there is still plenty of debate regarding implant biocompatibility, resorption rates and osteoinductive capabilities. We aim to present a series of cases that presented with a delay in bone neo-formation, secondary bone edema surrounding the interference screw and persistent anterior tibial pain. Our lot was comprised of 5 men and 4 women with an average age of 27.7 (22-31) years old and an average time from the initial surgery of 17.77 (14-21) months. The MRI showed persistent edema located on the tibial end of the graft in 8 of our patients and no signs of implant resorption. The CT images showed little to no signs of bone neo-formation around the screw and graft. The KT tests showed significant differences (3mm or higher) in 2 patients and the average KOOS was 85 (79.2-88.7). The real question that needs to be raised is how do classic PLLA screws add up when compared to the new generation of implants that contain β-tricalcium phosphate or hydroxyapatite. As the surgical techniques will develop to less and less invasive, the implants must also evolve such as to allow faster graft integration and bone formation, resulting in smaller convalescence. An important part in research will be played by national ligamentoplasty registries that are still emerging in smaller countries.

articleTitle: Microwave irradiation in preparation of dental biomaterials
abstract: Tooth minerals consist in hydroxyapatite, tricalcium phosphate, octacalcium phosphate and dicalcium phosphatdehydrate. Hydroxyapatite and related biomaterials can be obtained by autochthon methods and the aim of this work was to create bio-nanomaterials with dental applications using microwave irradiation technique. Microwave extraction process from bovine bones was performed at 100–190°C using 0.05M sodium hydroxide. Microwave assisted syntheses of hydroxyapatite were conducted at different values of pH and different temperatures, 90–120°C. The resulted biomaterials were characterized by X-ray diffraction XRD, Fourier transform infrared FT-IR, transmission and scanning microscopy, TEM and SEM and TG-DTA analysis.

articleTitle: Electric supply availability for the surgical luminaires
abstract: The power supply of the surgical luminaires represents an important source of risk for the patient's safety. The performance indicator for this system is availability. Considering the dedicated standards, there has been proposed a structure for the power supply system of a H-Surgical LED luminaire for which it is evaluated the availability, respectively the unavailability. It's presented a method of evaluation which considers the failure of all elements of system, independent events; down times may have some probability distributions. An application is conducted to illustrate the utilization of the method and to highlight the importance of the preventive maintenance tests.
